##: Coze (扣子), the ByteDance AI workspace desktop client; the vendor page is https://www.coze.cn/overview.

The page has no static download link: the Windows button is resolved at runtime inside a lazily loaded chunk of the coze-space SPA. The binaries themselves sit on a ByteDance TOS bucket at https://lf3-cdn-tos.bytegoofy.com/obj/tron-demo/7617773946401724698/<buildId>/<version>/win32-x64/Coze-v<version>-win32-x64.exe, the build id changes with every release (1.1.45 shipped as 517484147, 1.1.46 as 519480105), and the bucket refuses listing, so a version alone does not address a file.

The vendor publishes no index of those builds, and its own update feed (cloud.bytedance.net, see resources/app-update.yml inside the payload) only answers inside ByteDance. checkver therefore follows streaming-tool and reads microsoft/winget-pkgs: it takes the highest semver folder under manifests/b/ByteDance/Coze, prints that release's installer manifest, and the regex captures the build id and the version from the InstallerUrl line. The GitHub REST API is tried first and the plain HTML tree/blob pages are the fallback, because the unauthenticated API quota is shared per IP.

The pinned build is the newest one published (1.1.46, 2026-10-14); its SHA-256 equals winget's InstallerSha256 and the SHA-512 equals the base64 value in the latest.yml that ships beside the installer.

The installer is a 32-bit PE stub wrapping an NSIS-3 Unicode payload: $PLUGINSDIR\app-64.7z holds the app flat, with Coze.exe at the root, and $R0 only carries 'Uninstall Coze.exe'. The installer script expands the payload into $dir and drops both folders; the two app-shell PowerShell helpers in $PLUGINSDIR belong to the vendor's in-place upgrade path and are not needed here.
autoupdate.hash reads the electron-updater latest.yml that sits next to the installer in the same version folder, decoding its base64 sha512, so refreshing the digest costs no 187 MiB download.
description: AI agent workspace for coding, documents, slides and video projects (扣子)
notes: The NSIS stubs ($PLUGINSDIR and the bundled 'Uninstall Coze.exe') are dropped, so Scoop owns the uninstall.
Sign-in state, projects and the updater cache are written to "$env:APPDATA\Coze" and "$env:LOCALAPPDATA%\coze-updater", so nothing needs to be persisted.

The bundled shell updater stays enabled. An in-app update runs the vendor installer, which installs a per-user copy outside the Scoop app directory instead of replacing it; run 'scoop install coze -f' afterwards to return to the packaged build.
The 187 MiB download unpacks to a flat 600 MB directory that also carries app_shell_updater.exe and the vendor's app-shell upgrade helpers.
The desktop client can hand tasks to local agents such as Claude Code or Codex CLI, so those have to be installed separately if you want that part of the feature set.
